task: The INIT_CHECK gate decides on agentResults and issues inside init-check.json, but signInitCheck takes neither as input, so a hand-edited file remains signature-valid and the gate accepts it with zero init_check_set calls. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not inferred.
outcome:
A maintainer who edits agentResults in .lattice/story/actives/B-xxxx/init-check.json to add reviewer coverage nobody produced, then runs the advance, sees the gate refuse:

  $ lattice story_advance --storyId=B-xxxx --phase=INIT_CHECK
  Cannot enter INIT_CHECK: init-check.json _hash mismatch (agentResults/issues/background/title/description/checklist were modified); please re-run the lattice-review-story-init agent. [init_check_tampered]

  INIT_CHECK aborted: Story B-xxxx stays at INIT (phase not advanced; no worktree created).

Today the identical command instead prints 'Story B-xxxx advanced to INIT_CHECK' and creates the worktree. The parenthetical currently reads '(background/title/description/checklist were modified)' and must grow with the domain, since it is itself a fixed enumeration standing in for a property.
facts: EXECUTED PROOF (probe, 2 gate controls + 2 signature controls, 0 BROKEN): injecting a product-reviewer entry into agentResults with NO init_check_set call leaves the file signature-valid and the gate advances

EXECUTED PROOF: hand-erasing a recorded critical issue also leaves the file signature-valid and the gate advances, so issues is outside the domain too and fixing agentResults alone leaves an equivalent hole

EXECUTED CONTROL: editing an IN-DOMAIN field (title) DOES change the recomputed signature and IS rejected as init_check_tampered, ruling out the competing explanation that the signature check is simply dead
signInitCheck (core/init-check-gate.ts:133-143) signs storyId:backgroundHash:title:description:checklistHash:reviewRound:INIT_CHECK_SALT; agentResults and issues are absent
The existing tamper message at core/machine.ts:1144 enumerates the signature domain in its parenthetical, so the message text is bound to the domain and must change with it
store.readInitCheck (core/store.ts:566-572) is a bare readJson with no _hash verification; the carry-forward (handlers/init-check.ts:138-142) trusts it

IMPACT IS NARROWER THAN A FIRST READING SUGGESTS. Both tampering outcomes are ALREADY reachable through legal CLI calls: one caller can satisfy both required reviewers with two init_check_set calls, and a later call replaces a recorded critical issue with none. Both verified by execution. Tampering therefore grants NO capability that the legal path lacks

What tampering DOES add, measured: zero audit trail. A legal two-reviewer write left 9 durable records; the hand-injected second reviewer left 0. It also bypasses the actor registry, which refuses unregistered ids on the CLI path
Therefore the value of this story is audit integrity, not access control: a signed init-check.json currently implies tamper-evidence it does not deliver for the fields that matter

EXP-001's claim was RE-VERIFIED independently (4 samples, main x2 vs subagent x2): zero fields distinguish caller; the full environment digest is byte-identical and Lattice's derived sessionId is identical. PID/PPID vary per invocation for the SAME caller, so they carry no caller signal. The constraint against adding agentId validation is therefore sound

Measured at commit c59f9c0113: 637 init-check.json files; DONE 613 / DISCARDED 13 / INIT_CHECK 8 / INIT 1 / unreadable-index 2; only the INIT one is operationally gated (core/machine.ts:440 early-returns for non-INIT)

Six distinct on-disk agentResults shapes; ~195 of 637 files carry an actor absent from AGENT_DISPATCH_REGISTRY (chiefly the pre-rename koala-review-story-init), so no migration can re-sign the corpus through the handler
constraints: MUST NOT change whether one caller can invoke init_check_set twice with different registered agentIds. By design per EXP-001 (now independently re-verified) and asserted by four smoke tests
MUST NOT add agentId validation or caller-identity checks; the re-verification confirms no mechanical signal exists to validate against
MUST NOT attempt to re-sign the existing corpus by routing through the handler; ~195 files carry registry-invalid actors and would throw
MUST NOT touch packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/, red-w2c-v1-verdict-invariance.mjs, or red-b2aa7-chk007-receipt.mjs
MUST NOT push to any remote

MUST NOT claim, in any user-facing text or summary, that reviewer coverage becomes trustworthy. After this ships the gate proves only that the record was not edited outside the tool; a single caller can still legally self-satisfy both reviewer slots. Overstating this is worse than not fixing it
unknowns: What an absent agentResults field should hash to for the five legacy files where initCheckAgentResults synthesizes a single-element array from top-level agentId/issues
Whether a _hash mismatch on read should refuse the carry-forward only, or refuse the read entirely; the choice decides whether the audit-only majority of the corpus becomes unreadable
